reasons: Deviation is correctly identified: Section 4.1 auto-renews annually but requires ninety (90) days' notice to exit, exceeding both the 30-day preferred and 60-day fallback windows and sitting at the walk-away boundary; the one-year renewal term is properly flagged as acceptable.

Redline reaches the playbook position: Customer's non-renewal/termination notice is reduced to thirty (30) days (deterministic check confirms value=30 ≤ 60) and a sixty (60) day pre-renewal reminder from HDI is added, matching the preferred position's reminder requirement.
Leaving HDI's notice at ninety (90) days is pro-Customer (longer runway for us) and does not conflict with the rule, which governs Customer's exit window.
Correctly concludes no uplift cap is needed given the fixed 30% revenue-share fee structure with no price-escalation mechanism, so the rule's pricing element is not under-addressed.
Comment is accurate, concise, in first person plural with the required [Playbook] prefix, states what changed and why, and offers the 60-day fallback.

Changed-character ratio of 0.489 is justified: the single sentence conflated both parties' notice obligations and had to be restructured to differentiate our shortened window; party references use correct aliases (Company/HDI).
